c.h:
This guide describes the most effective pay to play methods to train the Woodcutting skill. The experience rate estimates in this guide do not incorporate the use of any experience boosting items or bonus experience and assume that the best possible hatchet is being used for the stated Woodcutting level. Woodcutting is a gathering skill which typically involves collecting logs from different types of trees.

While cutting ivy or trees (which grant logs), players have a chance of spawning a bird's nest. Bird's nests can contain rings, bird's eggs, raven eggs, seeds, and wood spirits. With the Grove of Fort Forinthry fully upgraded, nests containing seeds and rings will yield slightly improved loot, and rarely, some nests may contain pieces of the Imcando hatchet. The leftover nest can be crushed to obtain a crushed nest worth 234 gp. When chopping crystal trees, crystal geodes will drop instead of bird's nests, which can be shattered to obtain gems, crystal triskelion fragments, and crystal weapon seeds. When chopping eternal magic trees, enchanted bird's nest will occasionally drop along with other bird's nests.

Levelling up the Woodcutting skill increases the rate at which players gain resources and experience while woodcutting. As players level up they are also able to use better hatchets which are more efficient. To gain the best experience rates possible, players are strongly recommended to use the highest level hatchet available to them.

Hatchets are the primary tool used for Woodcutting. In addition to Woodcutting level requirements, hatchets require certain Attack levels to be wielded. However, players are able to use a hatchet without equipping it, as hatchets held in the inventory or tool belt are automatically used to cut wood. For non-augmentable hatchets, players are strongly advised to add their hatchet to their tool belt or equip it to save inventory space. Adding a hatchet of a higher tier to the tool belt will replace the current one, placing the previous one back in the player's inventory. Players can add a hatchet which they have a high enough Woodcutting level to use to their tool belt. It's recommended to always use the best hatchet available.

Certain hatchets can be augmented, allowing them to hold perks which can aid in Woodcutting. Even if not augmented, it is recommended to use augmentable hatchets available to your Woodcutting level if possible as they are 3 tiers more powerful than non-augmentable hatchets occupying the same level requirement (e.g. the dragon hatchet is functionally equivalent to a level 63 hatchet). These hatchets can only be added to the tool belt if they are not augmented, and can be freely removed from the tool belt for the purpose of augmentation at any time.

The inferno adze is a unique hybrid tool which functions similarly to a dragon hatchet and a rune pickaxe + 3, but has an added effect of instantly burning 1/3 of the logs chopped for Firemaking experience in addition to the Woodcutting experience. This tool cannot be augmented, nor can it be added to the tool belt.

Players with at least level 22 Invention can discover how to augment hatchets. This allows the player to create augmented crystal, dragon, imcando hatchets, augmented hatchet of ember and glade, and augmented hatchet of bloom and blight by using augmentors on their respective standard counterpart. Hatchets stored on the tool belt can be augmented after removing from it. Any augmented hatchets cannot be added to the tool belt.

c.h:
Wood boxes are storage items created through the Fletching skill which are used to help store logs, wood spirits, bird's nests, divine eggs and crystal geodes. They are very helpful when training Woodcutting, as they can greatly prolong the time spent cutting trees before needing to deposit logs at a bank.

Multiple wood boxes can be owned, but they all share the same stock of logs. If any one of the wood boxes is destroyed or lost, the logs would be retained in any other boxes still in the backpack; if there are none, the logs would disappear and only reappear in any wood boxes that are withdrawn to the backpack or newly created.

Wood boxes can be fletched from various tiers of logs, starting with basic logs and reaching all the way to Eternal magic logs. Each wood box upgrade requires 6 of the respective logs as well as the previous tier of wood box to fletch. Higher quality wood boxes can be created with higher Fletching levels, and can both store more logs and store higher tiers of logs compared to lower quality wood boxes. All wood boxes can be traded between players or purchased from the Grand Exchange.

At level 1 Woodcutting, players should begin training on regular trees. Between level 1 and 10 Woodcutting, players can gain up to 14,500 base experience per hour cutting regular trees. This experience rate assumes the player is using a dwarven army axe to gain additional Woodcutting experience. Regular trees are located just about everywhere throughout RuneScape. To avoid having to wait for trees to respawn while training, players should train in locations with many regular trees available (such as south-west of the Grand Exchange in Varrock, west of the Cooks' Guild). Players wishing to obtain more logs could use a Seers' headband 1 (or better) which gives a chance of obtaining two logs at once when cutting regular trees, though this does not give any additional experience. The Seers' headband is obtained from completing the easy Seers' Village achievements.

At level 10 Woodcutting players can start training on oak trees. Between level 10 and 20 Woodcutting, players can gain up to 19,000 base experience per hour cutting oak trees. Oak trees are found in many locations throughout RuneScape. Examples for good locations include east of Draynor Village bank, south-west of Varrock's west bank and north of the Yanille lodestone.

At level 20 Woodcutting players should begin training on willow trees. Between level 20 and 30 Woodcutting players can gain up to 27,000 base experience per hour cutting willow trees. One of the best locations to cut willow trees is just south-west of the bank in Draynor Village, where a large group of willow trees can be found on the coastline.

At level 30 Woodcutting, players can train on teak trees. Cutting teak trees at the Hardwood Grove near Tai Bwo Wannai on Karamja (accessible for a payment of 100 trading sticks) yields between 30,000 and 41,000 base experience per hour for Woodcutting levels 30-40. While cutting teak logs, there is a 2.5% chance of obtaining special teak logs, which can be used in Construction to convert teak logs into teak planks for free or traded to a Sawmill Operator for 1,300 gp each. Players with a combat level of 10 or less will be attacked by level 5 snakes in the grove. Players with at least level 6 Divination can use signs of the porter to bank teak logs, except for special teak logs. A near the teak trees on Ape Atoll, accessible after completing Deadliest Catch and starting Monkey Madness, is useful for efficient teak log banking.
cn: 5% chance of obtaining special teak logs, which can be used in Construction to convert teak logs into teak planks for free or traded to a Sawmill Operator for 1,300 gp each

c.h: At level 35 Woodcutting, players can begin chopping creeping ivy, found growing on walls on Havenhythe. There is one convenient location on the east wall of Isaac's house, directly north of the Wendlewick lodestone. Players can expect between 30,000 and 75,000 base experience per hour. Cutting ivy requires less effort and attention than cutting most other trees and so proves popular with some players. Cutting ivy doesn't provide any logs but still gives a chance to find bird's nests.

At level 40 Woodcutting, players can begin chopping maple trees. Between level 40 and 56 Woodcutting, players can gain from 40,000 to 55,000 base experience per hour cutting maple trees. One of the best locations to cut maple trees is in Seers' Village, where several maple trees are found close to a bank.

At level 56 Woodcutting, players can begin chopping arctic pines on Neitiznot, requiring starting The Fremennik Isles to access the island. Completing the quest is not required. Between level 56 and 58 Woodcutting, players can gain around 60,000 base experience per hour cutting arctic pines. If you don't have the Fremennik Isles unlocked, it may be faster to stick with maple until 58.

At level 58 Woodcutting, players can begin chopping eucalyptus trees around Oo'glog. Between level 58 and 60 Woodcutting, players can gain up to 62,000 base experience per hour cutting eucalyptus trees.

At level 60 Woodcutting, players can begin chopping mahogany, found in tropical areas across southern Karamja, Ape Atoll, and Mos Le'Harmless. From level 60 Woodcutting, players can gain around 63,000 experience per hour cutting mahogany. At 99 Woodcutting, players can gain 109,000 base experience per hour.

Players who have completed The Light Within (requires 80 Woodcutting) may want to continue cutting mahogany while using the Crystallise spell and the Light Form prayer. This requires level 88 Magic and 80 Prayer but provides the best Woodcutting experience rates all the way to level 99.

At level 68 Woodcutting, players can begin chopping choking ivy, found growing on walls in multiple locations including Varrock Palace, Falador, Yanille, Woodcutters' Grove, and the Crwys district of Prifddinas. Woodcutters' Grove will have six clumps of ivy available with the Grove upgraded to tier 2. Players can expect up to 86,000 base experience per hour. This can increase to up to 126,000 base experience per hour at level 99 Woodcutting. Cutting ivy requires less effort and attention than cutting most other trees and so proves popular with some players. Cutting ivy doesn't provide any logs but still gives a chance to find bird's nests.

Choking ivy can be found in several locations in RuneScape, though players who have access to Prifddinas are recommended to train at the choking ivy located in the Crwys district to take advantage of the Voice of Seren effect. Choking ivy can be found on the walls inside the greenhouse where Coeden is located. When the Voice of Seren is active in the Crwys district, base experience gained from chopping choking ivy there will be increased by 20%. Level 75 Woodcutting is required for Plague's End to unlock Prifddinas and chop choking ivy there.

At level 94 Woodcutting, players can cut crystal trees. Cutting crystal trees gives up to 130,000 base experience per hour at level 94 Woodcutting, and up to 133,000 base Woodcutting experience per hour at level 99 Woodcutting. Rates of over 200,000 Woodcutting experience per hour can be achieved at level 99 Woodcutting with the following boosts:

  • an augmented imcando hatchet with Honed 6 and Refined 4 in combination with an off-hand weapon with Wise 4
  • the Nature's sentinel outfit
  • the Ring of Whispers
  • Decorated woodcutting urns in combination with an urn enhancer
  • Perfect juju woodcutting potions
  • the Inspire Effort relic power
  • a Beaver familiar
  • the Clan avatar 6% experience boost

There are seven chop-able crystal trees in RuneScape, of which one at a time is active and can be cut. Players may locate the active crystal tree by travelling to any of the crystal trees and using the right-click option "Look at Crystal tree". This will inform the player of the direction that they need to travel in to find the active tree. Alternatively, players who have access to the Max Guild garden in Prifddinas (requiring at least one level 99 skill or ownership of a Quest Cape) may attune one of the skill portals found there to transport them directly to the active crystal tree (this is recommended in order to save time). The Nature's sentinel outfit can also teleport directly to the active crystal tree (up to 20 times per day, shared with the outfit's other teleports). The active crystal tree can be identified by it having a square of crystal shards around its base: these shards are chopped by the player to gain experience. As with ivy, crystal trees require little attention to train on and give no products to the player. The location of the active crystal tree changes every 2 hours.

At level 100 Woodcutting players should begin cutting eternal magic trees. These can be found in the middle of the Piscatoris Hunter area north of Eagle's Peak. Alternatively, they can be found at Dalia's Tree Nursery in Havenhythe after completing the achievements The Lute of Love and From Here to Eternity which is conveniently next to a bank chest after completing the achievement Trader Woes. Utilising the aforementioned boosts and equipment, upwards of 375,000 xp per hour can be gained from chopping these trees.

They behave quite differently from the majority of trees in the game:

  • Similar to elder trees, they remain standing for a set amount of time, with a minimum of 5 minutes until they are felled. The amount of time to felling is indicated by a green bar over the tree. When nobody is chopping the tree, the time to felling will slowly replenish back up to 5 minutes. Activations of the Refined perk and cadantine incense sticks will extend the felling time by 30 seconds up to a maximum of 5 times, which can extend the felling time by up to 2 minutes and 30 seconds.
  • There is a chance when cutting them to perform a Perfect Cut, which grants 5% extra experience and guarantees a log.
  • Periodically when cutting them they have a call to action mechanic where a ray of light and falling leaves will fall on one side of the tree. Chopping the tree on this side of the tree will grant Lumberjack's Intuition for 30 seconds, which provides multiple benefits (see the page for a full breakdown).
  • Between level 101 and 110 Woodcutting there are multiple levelling benefits that improve cutting eternal magic trees, including Lumberjack Intuition being more frequent and powerful, better base cutting rate, and increased chances of receiving enchanted bird's nests.
  • At level 110 Woodcutting, there is a small chance to receive a perfect eternal magic branch when cutting eternal magic trees. Two of these are used in the creation of the masterwork bow, but additional branches can be given to Heedi in exchange for Woodcutting experience equivalent to a medium prismatic lamp.

Players can gain Woodcutting experience while participating in the Evil Tree Distraction and Diversion. Evil trees can be chopped at all levels, depending on their type. With level 60 Woodcutting players can woodcut yew evil trees, at level 75 players can cut magic evil trees, and with at least level 90 players can cut elder evil trees. A player using a crystal hatchet with level 99 Woodcutting can expect experience rates equivalent to approximately 111,000 experience an hour cutting yew evil trees, 176,500 experience an hour cutting magic evil trees, and 219,500 experience an hour cutting elder evil trees. Components of the lumberjack outfit can be worn to increase the amount of experience that is gained from woodcutting an evil tree. As of the Dailyscape Overhaul, players no longer have a daily limit for interacting with evil trees.

Every 2 hours an evil tree sapling will appear in one of many possible locations across RuneScape; the time until an evil tree sapling spawning can be checked in the minigames tab of the Adventures interface. Players may identify the evil tree sapling's location by gaining a hint from a spirit tree. Once an evil tree sapling has grown into a tree players can speak to a spirit tree to be teleported directly to the evil tree. Players can nurture an evil tree sapling to receive Farming experience and to help it to grow into an evil tree. When an evil tree first appears it will have 100% health - the aim of the Distraction and Diversion is to destroy the evil tree by depleting all its health. To do this players must firstly cut down at least one of the 4 evil roots surrounding the evil tree, as these will knock players away from the evil tree while they are present. After cutting down an evil root the player can access the evil tree and woodcut it to deplete its health. Woodcutting experience is gained both from cutting the evil tree and its evil roots.

Each time that they cut down an evil root players gain evil tree kindling, which can be used to light fires in 8 spots around the base of the evil tree. Lighting fires decreases an evil tree's health more rapidly, so players wishing to maximise their Woodcutting experience gains may wish to avoid doing this to prolong the amount of time that can be spent woodcutting the tree. The amount of time taken to destroy an evil tree varies depending on the Woodcutting level required to woodcut the tree and the number of players assisting in depleting the tree's health. If you assist in cutting down an Evil Tree, you can receive a boost that auto-banks any logs cut and also increases the time for a tree to stay standing. Depending on the level of evil tree, the duration of the boost can be between 6–30 minutes.

Supply runs are a safe activity that take place on Mazcab every 12 hours (at midnight and noon game time). The activity begins with goebie supplies spawning at the supply rock near to Querci in Kanatah and is available until 25 minutes past the hour. Players may take up to 10 goebie supplies per day from the supply rock. Upon taking goebie supplies players become flagged for safe PvP and can be attacked by other players. Death results in the loss of all goebie supplies that the player is carrying. After obtaining goebie supplies players must travel north-west through the Nemi Forest to Otot, where the supplies may be exchanged for experience with Quercy. The player will be given a choice between two skills in which to gain experience: Agility or Crafting, Farming or Herblore and Hunter or Woodcutting. Different skills are offered on different worlds, so players may change worlds to find a world where the skill in which they wish to gain experience is offered.

Between 495 and 48,515 experience, at levels 1 and 99 respectively, can be gained from exchanging 10 goebie supplies. Assuming the activity is completed in 5 minutes, experience is awarded at a rate equivalent to between 5,940 and 582,180 experience an hour, at levels 1 and 99 respectively.

Players can use reward points from the Stealing Creation minigame to purchase proto-tools and volatile clay tools. These items can be transformed into a selection of skill related tools, including sacred clay hatchets and volatile clay hatchets. These hatchets can be right-clicked to grant Woodcutting bonus experience (it is not necessary for the hatchets to be equipped to gain bonus experience). Players are advised to play Stealing Creation with a group of players co-operating in non-combat games to deplete all sources of clay available more quickly. Once all the clay available in a game has been depleted the game will end early, allowing players to gain reward points in shorter amounts of time.

Both proto-tools and volatile clay tools cost 20 reward points per tool to purchase. When converting a proto-tool the player can choose which skilling tool it will become, but converting a volatile clay tool creates a random skilling tool. A volatile clay hatchet grants 29,340 Woodcutting bonus experience, while sacred clay hatchets grant 24,450 Woodcutting bonus experience. A skilling tool created from a volatile clay tool can be reverted back to the volatile clay tool and then converted again to potentially give a different tool. This may be done up to 10 times (the volatile clay tool is destroyed upon the 10th reversion); each reversion causing the tool formed from the volatile clay tool to have 10% less bonus experience available to be granted. Both sacred clay and volatile hatchets retain their form after being drained of bonus experience, and players can then use 20 reward points to recharge the depleted tools rather than purchasing new tools. Because of this players can maximise the amount of Woodcutting bonus experience they obtain from their reward points by initially purchasing a volatile clay tool and then transforming and reverting the skilling tools created until a volatile clay hatchet is obtained. Players can then continue recharging the volatile clay hatchet and claiming 29,340 Woodcutting bonus experience from it each time they obtain 20 reward points.

Players with at least level 80 in Woodcutting, Hunter, Fishing, and Mining will be able to gather clay from all possible locations in a game of Stealing Creation. With these levels players can gather enough clay during a game of Stealing Creation to gain 24 reward points per game that they play. Assuming games of Stealing Creation are completed in around 12 and a half minutes, players can complete 4.8 games of Stealing Creation per hour and earn 115.2 reward points per hour - enabling them to obtain 140,832 Woodcutting bonus experience an hour.
cn: Both proto-tools and volatile clay tools cost 20 reward points per tool to purchase

c.h: If you are in a clan with a woodcutting plot (tree) a substantial amount of Woodcutting experience can be gained weekly. This gives between 6,872 base experience per hour at level 1 and 96,500 at level 99 with rank 3 Fealty. This method is not the fastest, but it also allows you to activate the Clan Avatar Experience boost (See above). Additionally, contributing enough to the weekly upkeep of the Citadel gives players access to bonus experience from the Quartermaster in any skill for which the Citadel has a skill plot and is also enough to maintain the fealty bonus (for the following week).

In the Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup minigame, a machete is used to hack jungle, with various densities of being unlocked at levels 10, 20, and 35, giving experience similar to chopping trees at those levels. Thatch spars can be made into skewer sticks or used to repair rotten village fences for additional Woodcutting experience. Players also have a chance at receiving gems, three unique tribal masks, and the extremely valuable gout tuber. Playing the minigame awards Tai Bwo Favour, which can be used to enter the hardwood grove to chop teak trees and mahogany in a safe location without challenging quest requirements.

With at least level 50 Woodcutting, players may begin to cut acadia trees. This gives between 55,000 base experience an hour at level 50 and 117,000 base experience an hour at level 99. Acadia trees are found in west of Het's Oasis, Menaphos Imperial district or VIP skilling area, or north of Uzer. Partial completion of The Jack of Spades quest is required to access acadia trees located within Menaphos.

While cutting acadia trees in Menaphos, players will gain Menaphos reputation, which unlocks rewards within the city. At rank 2 reputation for the Imperial District, players can use a nearby bank deposit box. Until rank 2 has been achieved, it is advised to place the acadia logs in the action bar and drop them from there (players must still right click the action bar slot, but dropping them in this fashion does not interrupt cutting the tree, even if the animation pauses momentarily).

The VIP skilling area is unlocked at tier 7 overall reputation; acadia trees in this area deplete at half the rate of other acadia trees. At tier 8 Imperial District reputation, the player's success chance while cutting acadia trees is increased by up to 10%.

Crystallise and Light Form can be used on acadia trees after unlocking them through completing The Light Within quest, which has level 80 Woodcutting as a requirement. Be sure to wear prayer-boosting gear to lengthen Light Form, and to have a full inventory so you don't accidentally deplete the acadia tree resource. Note that a log-splitting scrimshaw will not provide a bonus while using this method given that you are not actually receiving any logs.

Players with level 83 Archaeology should consider using the Always Adze relic power while cutting acadia trees. This offers fast Firemaking XP and eliminates the need to bank or drop acquired logs.

Using the following items can net experience of around 250,000 experience an hour at level 90; Nature's sentinel outfit, perfect juju woodcutting potion, decorated woodcutting urns, Light Form alongside Crystallise, torstol incense sticks, and crystal skillchompas.

At level 81, players can train Woodcutting at the overgrown idols on Karamja and Anachronia. An idol is a statue surrounded by around 20 vines. Chopping vines gives XP for about 10 minutes until the vine has been cleared.

Idols provide around 100,000 XP an hour at level 81 woodcutting. Idols are an AFK method of training woodcutting, unlike using Crystallise and Light Form which requires attention every few seconds.

The fastest way to navigate to the idols is to tune the Skill portal in Max Guild to "Overgrown Idols". Players may enter this guild if they have 99 in any one skill. The same portal teleports players interchangeably between the two idols present in Karamja. One idol can be found south-west of the Shipyard entrance and another north of the Jadinko Lair.

Elder trees require much less attention as, unlike other trees, they run off of a 5 minute timer once the player starts chopping them. This timer is instanced for the player and is independent from others cutting the same tree. Once an elder tree has been depleted after the 5 minutes, players may use a superior locator to teleport to another elder tree (including the current tree that the player is at or ones that are still depleted). The Always Adze relic power or Superheat Form curse may be used to automatically burn the elder logs as they are chopped, eliminating the need for banking or porters, as well as granting Firemaking experience. If Superheat Form is used, the player should bring prayer potions and an ancient elven ritual shard to upkeep prayer points. Alternatively, an Orthen furnace core may be equipped to use Superheat Form without draining prayer points, although the player will lose the benefits of Sana's fyrtorch if they own one. A grace of the elves enchanted with the Dark Facet of Grace may also be used to eliminate the prayer drain of Superheat Form, allowing the use of Sana's fyrtorch.

Golden bamboo trees are a rare Woodcutting resource that can be found randomly on Uncharted Isles. Uncharted Isles can be explored from the The Arc region, which requires completion of the Impressing the Locals quest to access. Completion of the Flag Fall miniquest, which allows the player to claim an uncharted isle and return to it, is also required to woodcut golden bamboo effectively. To find golden bamboo trees, the player must first gain some chimes from skilling in The Arc so that they can purchase the supplies required to voyage to Uncharted Isles. Supplies can be purchased from Rosie (supplies). When the player finds an Uncharted Isle with golden bamboo trees then they can claim the island using a claim island flag. Once an uncharted isle is claimed the player may return to it for the price of 3 supplies per voyage: 5 supplies can be claimed per day for free from the box next to Rosie. Up to 3 golden bamboo trees may be present on an Uncharted Isle, if the player opts to go on a long voyage.

Golden bamboo can be cut with level 96 Woodcutting. Each day the player may cut approximately 100 golden bamboo per tree before it is depleted. The daily cap resets at 00:00 UTC. Depleting one tree takes around 30 minutes. When selling the golden bamboo gained from woodcutting players can expect to gain enough chimes to cover the cost of purchasing supplies to go on additional long voyages to find more golden bamboo trees and thus woodcut from them indefinitely. Purchasing the supplies cost reductions and commodity sell price increases unlocks from the Waiko Reward Shop, in addition to having a claimed island with as many golden bamboo trees as possible, will further increase the viability of searching for more trees to woodcut continuously. At level 99, woodcutting golden bamboo gives an experience rate equivalent to around 300,000 Woodcutting experience an hour. Assuming it is cut continuously and not accounting for time spent finding further bamboo.

Note: A single golden bamboo plant may take anywhere from 30 minutes to an hour to be depleted. This will affect experience rates. At 110 Woodcutting, utilising urns, perfect juju woodcutting potions, beaver familiars, a log splitting scrimshaw, BIS (best in slot) Hatchets (with perks Honed and or Naturalist), Nature's sentinel outfit, and Sana's fyrtorch, experience rates can exceed 776,000 Woodcutting experience per hour. Lastly, Brawling gloves (Woodcutting) is another method for boosting experience.

The experience from woodcutting golden bamboo can further be bolstered by completing contracts given by Sojobo (contracts) on Waiko or via a contract contact on an Uncharted Isle. Players may complete up to 3 contracts daily, and may purchase upgrades from Boni for a maximum of 7 daily contracts. Doing contracts, however, requires chimes to be able to reroll contracts until satisfactory golden bamboo ones are assigned.

This guide describes the most effective non-members methods to train the Woodcutting skill. The experience rate estimates in this guide do not incorporate the use any experience boosting items or bonus experience and assume that players are using the best possible hatchet available for their Woodcutting level. Woodcutting is a gathering skill which, for free-to-play players, involves obtaining logs by chopping trees. Only 7 different types of tree are available to non-members: trees, oak trees, willow trees, teak, maple trees, acadia trees and yew trees. Hatchets are tools required to chop trees. As players level up their Woodcutting skill they are able to gain experience and logs more frequently while woodcutting. They are also able to use hatchets which cut at a faster rate. They can also cut more varieties of trees.

In addition to Woodcutting level requirements, hatchets require certain Attack levels to be wielded. However, players are able to use a hatchet without equipping it, as hatchets held in the inventory or tool belt are automatically used to chop. To save inventory space, players are strongly advised to add their hatchet to their tool belt or equip it. Once a hatchet is added to the tool belt it cannot be removed, but players can add a higher level hatchet to their tool belt if the hatchet currently stored in the tool belt is inferior to the one being added. Players can add hatchets which they do not currently have a high enough Woodcutting level to use to their tool belt, in which case they will function as the best available hatchet at the player's current Woodcutting level.

Hatchets can be purchased from the Grand Exchange, obtained as monster drops or smithed with the required Smithing level. Hatchets up to Adamant may also be bought from Bob's Brilliant Axes in Lumbridge.

Wood boxes can hold a large amount of logs, reducing the need for banking. Free players can use up to the acadia wood box, which holds logs up to acadia logs. It has a capacity of 120-230, depending on Woodcutting level. Wood boxes can be filled by logs in the backpack without interrupting woodcutting, and can then be emptied at a bank.

Urns can be used to gain additional Woodcutting experience while training. When held in the backpack, urns are filled as the player cuts trees. Only gains in base experience count towards filling an urn. Full urns can be teleported away to receive additional experience, equivalent to 20% of the Woodcutting experience gained while filling the urn. Only one urn is filled at a time, though players may own up to a total of 10 full urns.

Urns are only tradeable in their "no rune" forms. In order to use a woodcutting urn, the player must add an earth rune to it; this makes the urn untradeable.

If a player owns 10 full Woodcutting urns they must teleport at least 1 away before they can fill more urns. This can be sped up by automatically teleporting them - see Settings > Gameplay > Interfaces > Inventory.

Instead of dropping logs or sacrificing experience rates to bank them, players can use magic notepaper to note logs in their inventories. This gives less profit per log than regular banking, but allows for optimal experience rates to be maintained. Each log noted will use 1 magic notepaper, so subtract the current Grand Exchange price of the notepaper (529 gp) from the price of the logs for the profit per log.

Incense sticks can be consumed to give bonus effects for Woodcutting. Each incense stick consumed provides 10 minutes of the effect, which can be extended by consuming more sticks. When incense effects are active their potency increases every 10 minutes up to potency 4, which multiplies the effect's strength up to 4 times. Alternatively, 6 sticks can be consumed at once via the 'overload' right click option, skipping straight to potency 4. Guam incense sticks give a 10% chance, per potency level, to gain additional logs from regular trees.

Parts of the sentinel outfits can be crafted as a members by combining sentinel fragments with level 80 Woodcutting and 20 Invention.

The oaken, willow, and maple sentinel outfits are free-to-play equipments, which consist of head slot, body slot, leg slot, hand slot and feet slot items. When wearing a complete version of any of these three outfits, players gain the following bonuses:

  • 5 daily teleports to various woodcutting locations:
    • Trees: west Varrock and east Varrock
    • Oak trees: west Varrock and east Varrock
    • Willow trees: Draynor Village and Marigold Farm
    • Teak trees: Musa Point
    • Maple trees: Daemonheim Peninsula Island and south Varrock
    • Acadia trees: Het's Oasis
    • Yew trees: Edgeville and Varrock Palace
  • 5% increase success chance while Woodcutting.
  • An option to automatically burn logs when cut (25% chance).
  • The ability to contact Evil Trees (similar to the sunbeam crown).

Players who own all pieces of the oaken, willow, and maple sentinel outfits can combine these outfits' components to form the nature's sentinel outfit, which is also available to free-to-play players. This outfit gives superior benefits to those given by the other sentinel outfits:

  • 7% increased success chance while Woodcutting (as opposed to 5% with the other sentinel outfits).
  • 20 daily teleports (as opposed to 5 with the other sentinel outfits):
    • All teleport options that the other sentinel outfits offer
    • Active Evil Tree

At level 1 Woodcutting, players should begin training on regular trees. Between level 1 and 10 Woodcutting, players can gain experience at a rate equivalent to 9,700 experience per hour cutting regular trees. However, as only 1,154 experience is needed to achieve level 10 Woodcutting, a player starting with no Woodcutting experience can expect to achieve level 10 after around 8 minutes of training. This process can be further sped up by wielding a dwarven army axe, which grants additional experience per log cut. Regular trees are located throughout RuneScape. To avoid having to wait for trees to respawn while training, players should train in locations with many regular trees available (such as the dead trees to the south-west of the Grand Exchange in Varrock, west of the Cooks' Guild).

At level 10 Woodcutting players can start training on oak trees. Between level 10 and 20 Woodcutting, players can gain experience at a rate equivalent to 18,000 experience per hour at oak trees. As a total of around 3,316 Woodcutting experience is needed to advance from level 10 to 20 Woodcutting, players should be able to achieve these levels in approximately 11 minutes. Oak trees are found in many locations throughout Gielinor, but an example of a good place to cut them is just south-west of Varrock west bank (south of the Grand Exchange and just east of Gertrude's house). Here players will find 3 oak trees located close to the bank, with a further 3 oak trees located south of the first group.

At level 20 Woodcutting players should begin training on willows. One of the best locations to cut willow trees is just south-west of the Draynor bank, where a large group of willow trees can be found near the coast.

The willow wood box can hold 90-200 logs from willow or below. This, coupled with the Draynor willows' proximity to the bank, makes banking very easy. On free-to-play worlds, the willow wood box only holds 200 logs, not 230. The upgrades to get to 230 are members only.

Acadia trees are found north of Al Kharid and west of Het's Oasis, near the fire altar. There are multiple banks to choose from, the nearest being at the Kharid-et Dig Site. To minimise banking time, a quick bank access such as War's Retreat Teleport can be used, followed by fire altar teleport tablets.

Should the player expect to become a member in the future for long enough to unlock the Invention skill, saving all their cut acadia logs to disassemble is a highly efficient source of simple parts needed for divine charges.
